text: So King Solomon ruled over all Israel.
These were his high officials: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, the record keeper;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada, commander of the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
Azariah son of Nathan, in charge of the district governors; Zabud son of Nathan, priest and friend of the king;
Ahishar, in charge of the palace; and Adoniram son of Abda, in charge of the forced labor.
Solomon had twelve district governors over all Israel, who supplied provisions for the king and his household. Each one was responsible for one month of the year.
These are their names: Ben-Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
Ben-Deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan;
Ben-Hesed, in Arubboth—Socoh and all the land of Hepher were his;
Ben-Abinadab, in all of Naphath Dor—he had Solomon's daughter Taphath as his wife;
Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and all of Beth Shan, which lies beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth Shan to Abel Meholah and over as far as Jokmeam;
Ben-Geber, in Ramoth Gilead—the settlements of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead were his, as well as the region of Argob in Bashan, sixty large cities with walls and bronze bars on their gates;

versions.text: Ben-Geber, in Ramoth Gilead—the settlements of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead were his, as well as the region of Argob in Bashan, sixty large cities with walls and bronze gate bars;
versions.explanation: "Bronze gate bars" is compact but slightly clumsy to read aloud; "bronze bars on their gates" flows more naturally and conveys the same sense.

text: Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali—he too had married a daughter of Solomon, Basemath;
Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. He was the one governor over that land.

versions.text: Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. He was the only governor over that land.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew simply says "one governor who was in the land"; "the only governor" is an interpretive expansion. A footnote could note the ambiguity, or the wording could be kept closer to the Hebrew.

text: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore; they ate and drank and rejoiced.

versions.text: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore; they ate and drank and were content.
versions.explanation: The participle שְׂמֵחִים means "rejoicing, glad," a stronger note of joy than "were content." "Rejoiced" also gives a better closing cadence for oral reading.
